newsitem.title: CHINA: China says March trade surplus at $2.95 bln.
newsitem.headline: China says March trade surplus at $2.95 bln.

text.p: China posted a $2.95 billion trade surplus in March compared with a deficit of $728 million last year, the International Business Daily said on Tuesday.
The newspaper said exports for the month reached $14.05 billion, soaring 34.9 percent over the same month last year, while imports were 11.1 billion, down 0.2 percent.
China said on Monday it had a first quarter surplus of $6.71 billion compared with a $1.1 billion deficit in the first quarter of 1996.

In the first quarter, exports of industrial goods reached $30.6 billion, up 27.4 percent, while exports of primary agricultural products were $4.9 billion, an increase of 16.1 percent, the International Business Daily, published by the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, said.
Machinery exports reached $11.1 billion in the quarter, up 22 percent, while exports of clothing and other related goods reached $5.9 billion for a gain of 41 percent.
Exports of crude oil were worth $590 million, up 22 percent in value terms.
The newspaper said there were encouraging signs for state-owned enterprises as their exports climbed 25.7 percent to $20.1 billion in the quarter, outpacing the growth of foreign-invested firms.
Exports of foreign-invested firms, which have been a key engine of export growth in recent years, rose 23.7 percent to $14.4 billion.
Imports in the quarter showed a particularly sharp decline in the machinery sector where the total was down 13.7 percent to $11.5 billion.
Imports of machinery by foreign-invested companies fell 24.8 percent to $3.6 billion.
China ended duty-free treatment of imported capital equipment for foreign-funded firms in the second quarter of last year.
Imports of steel fell to 2.79 million tonnes, down 17.5 percent while imports of crude oil were 7.28 million tonnes, down 54.8 percent.
